title: Jordan's 'Last Dance' jersey nets record £10.6m at auction
title_zh: 乔丹“最后一舞”球衣拍出创纪录的1060万英镑

image.credit: Photo by Keith Christian Armada on Unsplash
image.author: Keith Christian Armada

lead: A Michael Jordan jersey from his final championship season has fetched $14 million, setting a new benchmark for basketball memorabilia. The sale underscores the soaring value of sports relics once owned by iconic athletes.
lead_zh: 迈克尔·乔丹在其最后一个夺冠赛季所穿的一件球衣以1400万美元成交，刷新了篮球纪念品的拍卖纪录。此次交易凸显了体育传奇人物旧物的价值正不断飙升。

preview_zh: 这件球衣是乔丹在1998年NBA总决赛第二场比赛中穿过的，并附有他的亲笔签名，最终以1400万美元（约1060万英镑）成交，创下篮球纪念品的拍卖纪录。当晚，乔丹砍下全场最高的37分，随后以4比2的总比分赢得系列赛，为他在芝加哥公牛队的最后一个赛季画上句号，也夺得了他第六个也是最后
paragraphs: The jersey, worn by Jordan during game two of the 1998 NBA Finals and personally autographed, sold for $14 million (£10.6 million), a record for any piece of basketball memorabilia. That evening, Jordan poured in a game-high 37 points before capping his final season with the Chicago Bulls by clinching a 4-2 series victory and his sixth and last NBA Championship. He was named Finals MVP on all six occasions.

Only one item of sports memorabilia has ever commanded a higher price: the jersey worn by baseball legend Babe Ruth when he 'called the shot' in the 1932 World Series, which fetched $24.1 million (£18.2 million) in 2024. The previous basketball record had been held by a 2007-08 card featuring both Jordan and Kobe Bryant, which sold for $12.9 million (£9.8 million) last year.

The record for a game-worn Jordan item had been set merely two weeks earlier, when his unautographed jersey from game three of the 1998 Finals went under the hammer for $12.3 million (£9.3 million). The latest acquisition was made by Miami real estate investor Ron Firman in a private sale brokered by Hunt Auctions.

David Hunt, president of Hunt Auctions, remarked in a statement: 'While Michael Jordan's importance within the sports memorabilia marketplace has long been established, it has now escalated to an elite asset class more typically reserved for iconic works of art.'
paragraphs_zh: 这件球衣是乔丹在1998年NBA总决赛第二场比赛中穿过的，并附有他的亲笔签名，最终以1400万美元（约1060万英镑）成交，创下篮球纪念品的拍卖纪录。当晚，乔丹砍下全场最高的37分，随后以4比2的总比分赢得系列赛，为他在芝加哥公牛队的最后一个赛季画上句号，也夺得了他第六个也是最后一个NBA总冠军。他六次均当选总决赛最有价值球员。
体育纪念品中只有一件曾拍出更高价格：棒球传奇人物贝比·鲁斯在1932年世界大赛中“预言本垒打”时所穿的球衣，于2024年以2410万美元（约1820万英镑）售出。此前的篮球纪念品纪录由一张2007-08赛季的乔丹与科比·布莱恩特双人卡保持，该卡去年以1290万美元（约980万英镑）成交。
乔丹比赛穿过的物品的拍卖纪录仅仅在两周前才被刷新，当时他在1998年总决赛第三场穿过的无签名球衣以1230万美元（约930万英镑）落槌。最新这件球衣由迈阿密房地产投资者罗恩·菲尔曼通过亨特拍卖行私下交易购得。
亨特拍卖行总裁大卫·亨特在一份声明中表示：“迈克尔·乔丹在体育纪念品市场中的重要性早已确立，如今它已升级为一种精英资产类别，通常只有标志性艺术作品才享有这种地位。”

title_original: Jordan 'Last Dance' jersey sells for record £10.6m
summary_original: A Michael Jordan jersey from his 'Last Dance' season sells for $14m (£10.6m), a record for a piece of basketball memorabilia.
body_original:
Jordan 'Last Dance' jersey sells for record £10.6m
By
Ben Collins
BBC Sport journalist
Published
5 hours ago
A Michael Jordan jersey from his 'Last Dance' season has sold for $14m (£10.6m), a record for a piece of basketball memorabilia.
Jordan wore the Chicago Bulls jersey during game two of the 1998 NBA Finals and has autographed it too.
He scored a game-high 37 points that evening before ending his last season with the Bulls with a 4-2 series win for his sixth and final NBA Championship. He was named the Finals' Most Valuable Player in all six.
The only item of sports memorabilia that has cost more is the jersey worn by baseball legend Babe Ruth when he "called the shot" during the 1932 World Series, which was sold for $24.1m (£18.2m) in 2024.
The previous high for a basketball item was a card featuring Jordan and Kobe Bryant from 2007-08 which
sold for $12.9m (£9.8m) last year.
The previous record for a piece of game-worn Jordan memorabilia was set just two weeks ago when his jersey from game three of the 1998 Finals, which is not autographed,
sold via auction for $12.3m (£9.3m).
The latest purchase was made by Miami real estate investor Ron Firman in a private sale through Hunt Auctions.
David Hunt, president of Hunt Auctions, said in a statement: "While Michael Jordan's importance within the sports memorabilia marketplace has long been established, it has now escalated to an elite asset class more typically reserved for iconic works of art."
